_meta.purpose: Read-only reference snapshot of the four SLC Windows Scheduled Task definitions, captured directly from Get-ScheduledTask on 2026-08-28 (sleep-fix deployment: adds the new Schedule Health Check task; also captures WakeToRun/StartWhenAvailable/LogonType/RunLevel, which the 2026-08-17 snapshot did not record).
_meta.why_this_exists: run_hidden.vbs is Tier-2 guardrail-hashed (see live_slc/guardrails.py), but a file hash only protects the launcher script's own bytes. Each Scheduled Task passes the target .bat file as a runtime Arguments string configured entirely inside Windows Task Scheduler - that configuration is not a repo file and is not reachable by any file-hash system. This snapshot is the only protection against that configuration silently drifting (e.g. a task repointed at the wrong .bat, an argument edited outside this process, or a wake/catch-up setting silently flipped).
_meta.enforcement: Manual re-diff only, against a fresh `Get-ScheduledTask` read. Not automated, not hash-verified, not checked by any Python code.
_meta.captured_by: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName <name> | Select-Object State, Actions, Triggers, Settings, Principal
_meta.notable_finding: The Cycle task has StartWhenAvailable=False (Preflight and Closeout are both True). A cycle slot missed while the machine is asleep is never caught up after waking - it is permanently lost for that day - while a late Preflight or Closeout eventually still fires. This is consistent with the exact partial-coverage pattern (58/72, 60/72 cycles) that motivated this deployment: the machine woke mid-session, Preflight/Closeout caught up late, but every cycle slot during the sleep window was gone for good.

TradingBot SLC Schedule Health Check.note: Newly registered as part of the sleep-fix deployment. Registered disabled deliberately - enabled together with the other three as the final deployment step, never live while the original three are still off.
